## Summary

`wl sync`'s merge logic can enter a self-sustaining conflict loop that silently corrupts item state. Observed in the field (LP-0MSDRRPV0001TCLX in /home/rgardler/projects/llm): a completed, audit-approved item's local `updatedAt` advanced at every sync (21:36:19Z → 21:53:40Z → 21:57:35Z) and the final sync chose a local `deleted` state (empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`) over the remote `open` state — soft-deleting the item while the remote `worklog/data` ref still had it `open`/`plan_complete`. No agent ran `wl delete`; the state arose purely from merge behavior. The item had to be manually restored via `StatusLifecycle`.

## Root-cause hypothesis (verified against src/sync.ts)

1. **Same-timestamp merge bumps `updatedAt` unconditionally.** `mergeSameTimestampItems` (src/sync.ts ~L423) sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content (e.g. a `sortIndex` conflict from concurrent `wl re-sort`, or any divergent field). This bump makes the item *newer* than the remote on the next sync, so the local value keeps winning and the timestamp keeps advancing on every sync — a conflict loop with no real user edit behind it. Under auto-sync / multi-pane / multi-agent use this can repeat indefinitely.

2. **Unattributed soft-delete wins over a live remote item.** `deleteSingle` (node_modules/@worklog/shared/src/database.ts) sets `status: 'deleted'` but leaves `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` empty. In `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`, `status` is resolved by plain timestamp recency: `status='deleted'` is a non-default value, so if the local copy is (artifactually) newer, `status` flips to `deleted` even though `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` are empty — silently soft-deleting an item the remote still considers open. There is no delete-side equivalent of the close-preservation logic that protects `status='completed'`/`stage='done'`.

## Expected behaviour

- Repeated syncs of the same divergent state must converge: once both sides hold the merged item, `updatedAt` must stop advancing and the item must not flip-flop.
- An unattributed delete marker (status='deleted' with empty deletedBy/deleteReason) must never override a remote item that is open/in-progress/completed. Deletes should only propagate when they are real, attributed deletes (non-empty deletedBy or deleteReason), mirroring the close-preservation model.

## Suggested approach

- In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, only bump `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field (or converge without bumping when the merged result equals one side). Consider whether `sortIndex` conflicts alone should bump at all.
- Add delete-side protection in `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` (and same-timestamp path): treat `status='deleted'` like `status='completed'` — require the delete to be the newer change AND attributed (deletedBy/deleteReason non-empty) before propagating it; otherwise keep the remote live status.
- Add regression tests in tests/sync.test.ts reproducing both failure modes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing only in `sortIndex` or one metadata field) synced repeatedly converge — `updatedAt` stops advancing after the merged state is present on both sides (no unbounded bumping).
- AC2: Regression test: local `status='deleted'` with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` vs remote `status='open'` — merge keeps the remote `open` state (or at minimum never produces a soft-deleted item with no attribution).
- AC3: Regression test: an *attributed* delete (non-empty `deletedBy`) that is newer than the remote still propagates (delete remains possible when intentional).
- AC4: Full existing test suite (npm test) passes with no regressions.
data.title: Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely and unattributed soft-delete wins over remote open item

# Prevent top line info bar from scrolling off screen (WL-0MSNI6TQ5003JY1Z)

## Headline

Fix the Herdr plugin's top `Work Items` info bar wrapping off screen in narrow panes by truncating the header to the terminal width so it never exceeds one row.

## Problem statement

In the Herdr `worklog-selection-list` plugin's list mode, the top info bar (row 0: `Work Items — N item(s) [auto-refresh on] [Downtime Off]` plus optional `(filtered: …)`, `(top …)`, `[paused — hidden]` and code-freeze banners) can exceed the pane width in narrow terminals. The header is assembled by string concatenation without truncation, so when its visible length exceeds `cols` the terminal wraps it onto extra physical rows. When total rendered output then exceeds the `rows - 1` line-count invariant (WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO), the terminal scrolls the first line off the top of the pane and the header is not visible — even with the minimal `[Downtime Off]` status and no idle timestamp.

## Users

- **Herdr worklist users** browsing the selection list in narrow panes (e.g. 80 cols or less, `herdr pane layout` narrow split), who rely on the top bar to see the item count, active filter, auto-refresh and downtime state.

### Example User Stories

- As a Herdr user with a narrow pane and many items, I want the top `Work Items` info bar to stay visible at row 0 regardless of pane width or list content, so I don't lose the item count and system status.
- As a Herdr user, I want a long header (filter + auto-refresh + downtime) to be truncated with an ellipsis rather than wrapping onto a second row and pushing the header off screen.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Header never wraps / always visible at row 0:** In list mode, the header line is truncated to fit the terminal width (visible length ≤ `cols`, ANSI preserved via `truncateLine`) so it occupies exactly one output row. For any `cols` ≥ 40 and any combination of `filterLabel`, `totalCount` (`top N of M`), `autoRefresh`, `panePaused`, and `downtimeStatus` (`[Downtime Off]`, `[Downtime Off (restored)]`, `[downtime paused]`, `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]`, `[downtime busy]`, `[⏳ downtime dispatching]`), `renderer(…)` output satisfies `stripAnsi(output.split('
')[0]).includes('Work Items')` and `stripAnsi(output.split('
')[0]).length <= cols`.

2. **Line-count invariant holds in narrow panes:** In list mode the full renderer output contains at most `rows - 1` newline-separated lines for any `TermSize` (e.g. 40×24, 80×24, 120×53, 60×20) and any list state (short list, full list, scrolled list, with/without banners, with/without fold indicators `▲/▼ more`, with minimal and maximal header length). No render exceeds the pane height and the top line is never scrolled off.

3. **No regression in other modes:** Detail-mode rendering (`formatDetailView` and renderer detail path with pinned header+ToC) and filter-mode rendering are unchanged — existing tests for the pinned ToC (WL-0MSI28AP80002F5S / WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I), `'keeps the ToC pinned at the top while the document scrolls'`, and filter prompt still pass with no behavior change.

4. **Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`:** Cover (a) header truncation at narrow width — visible length ≤ `cols` and `Work Items` text still present for a long header at 40 cols and 60 cols; (b) line-count invariant (`lines.length <= rows - 1`) for list mode at narrow width (40×24) with a long header, with banner active, and without banner; (c) wide-pane sanity (80×24 / 120×24) still passes — no over-truncation for short headers.

5. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any relevant README/docs entries describing the header layout (`packages/herdr/README.md`).**

6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Surgical fix in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `createListRenderer` list-mode header path only — do not change detail/filter rendering or the dynamic list/metadata panel layout beyond the header fix.
- Reuse the existing `truncateLine(line, maxWidth)` helper (ANSI-aware) — no new dependencies or truncation implementations.
- Preserve ANSI styling (bold Work Items, dim/colour for status segments) when truncating; the ellipsis `…` must close open ANSI codes via `ANSI.reset` as `truncateLine` already does.
- Must preserve the `rows - 1` invariant from WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO — the fix must not add chrome rows; the header must remain a single chrome row.
- No change to `renderDowntimeStatus` idle timer growth — truncation must remain correct as the `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]` string grows (regression guard).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `createListRenderer` (around lines 3217–3229) builds the list-mode header:
  ```ts
  let header = ` ${ANSI.bold}Work Items${ANSI.reset} — ${totalItems} item(s)${filterLabel}`;
  if (totalCount !== undefined && totalCount > totalItems) { header += ` (top ${totalItems} of ${totalCount})`; }
  if (autoRefresh) { header += ` ${ANSI.dim}[auto-refresh on]${ANSI.reset}`; }
  if (panePaused) { header += ` ${ANSI.fg(220)}[paused — hidden]${ANSI.reset}`; }
  if (downtimeStatus) { header += downtimeStatus; }
  output.push(header);
  ```
  The header is pushed without `truncateLine(…, cols)`, unlike banners (`truncateLine(bannerLine, cols)`) and footer/tooltip lines. When `visibleLength(header) > cols`, the pty wraps it onto a second physical row so `output` logically has `rows - 1` lines but physically occupies `rows` or more, scrolling the first line off the top (observed in narrow panes even with minimal `[Downtime Off]` content, and exacerbated by `codeFreezeActive` banners, long `filterLabel` like `(filtered: stage in_review)`, or large `totalCount`).

- Detail view header/ToC is already pinned (WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I / WL-0MSI28AP80002F5S): `formatDetailView` pins `DETAIL_HEADER_LINES + tocLines` at the top and only the body scrolls — not affected by this list-mode header issue.

- Prior fix WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO corrected layout accounting for group separators and notification-line overflow, and WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ accounted for `▲/▼ more` indicators in the `budgetForRows` budget — but neither guarded the header's own width.

- `truncateLine` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:1224`) is ANSI-aware and already used for banners; `renderDowntimeStatus` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:3077`) returns ANSI-wrapped status strings of varying length.

- No existing tests assert the header's visible length constraint at narrow widths; the overflow only appears visually in the pty and is not caught by current line-count tests which use wide (80/253) cols.

## Desired change

1. In `createListRenderer` list-mode branch (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` ~3220–3233), apply the existing `truncateLine` to the assembled header before pushing it:
   ```ts
   header = truncateLine(header, cols);
   output.push(header);
   ```
   (Keep the existing `output.push` as a single row; do not add a second header row.)

2. Verify the fix maintains the `rows - 1` invariant when the header is long — the header now costs exactly one line regardless of `cols`, so no additional chrome accounting is needed, but the safety clamp at the end of the renderer (`while (output.length > rows - 1) output.pop()`) remains as a backstop.

3. Do not change `renderDowntimeStatus`, `computeDynamicLayout`, `formatDetailView`, or the detail/filter render paths.

4. Update code comments on the header assembly to note the truncation guard and narrow-pane wrap prevention (reference this work item and WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO).

5. Add narrow-pane unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` per AC 4 and ensure all existing tests remain green.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `createListRenderer` list-mode header assembly (`Work Items …` concatenation and `output.push(header)`) and `truncateLine` helper; primary fix location.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Add header truncation and narrow-pane `rows - 1` invariant tests (list mode, with/without banners, varying header lengths); keep existing detail pinned-ToC tests green.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Update if it describes the header/status bar layout; otherwise code-comments only.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO** — "Herdr plugin: selection list header and top lines cut off top of pane" (completed, critical) — introduced the `rows - 1` / `rows` line-count invariant and corrected separator/notification accounting; this item extends the same invariant to the header's own width.
- **WL-0MSI28AP80002F5S** — "Detail view ToC overflows pane — first lines scroll off the top of the screen" (completed) — the detail-view analogue with pinned header+ToC; this list-mode header fix is the list-mode counterpart and must not regress that fix.
- **WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I** — "Detail view ToC for Related Docs" (completed) — introduced the pinned ToC design preserved by the previous item.
- **WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ** — "Herdr selection list: no indication of items below the fold" (completed) — introduced `▲/▼ more` indicators with explicit `budgetForRows - indicatorRows` accounting; relevant to the chrome budget near the header.
- **WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J** — "Herdr selection list: let list take as much space as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls" (completed) — introduced `computeDynamicLayout` and the `chromeLines = 2 + bannerCount` budget that the header consumes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: Over-truncation hides useful status.** Mitigation: `truncateLine` preserves the leading `Work Items — N item(s)` prefix and only drops trailing status segments; at 40 cols the most informative prefix remains visible and full status is available in wider panes. Document the truncation behavior.
- **Risk: `truncateLine` double-counts ANSI vs display width.** Mitigation: reuse the proven `truncateLine` implementation already used for banners; add a test that asserts visible length (via `stripAnsi`) after truncation, not raw string length.
- **Risk: Growing idle timer (`m:ss`) eventually pushes other segments off.** Mitigation: tested as part of the variable-length `downtimeStatus` combinations; the truncation guard is independent of which status variant is active.
- **Risk: Breaking existing line-count tests that assume header length.** Mitigation: widen the test cols or update expectations to account for truncation — no functional change for 80+ cols where the header already fits.
- **Assumption:** The reported wrap is in **list mode** (the main `Work Items` list), not in detail mode — confirmed by operator (Q4/Q5). If detail-mode header wrapping is later reported, a separate item should cover it.
- **Assumption:** Narrow pane is the primary reproduction (`cols ~ 40–80`); the fix is validated at 40 cols as the lower bound (below 40 the pane is pathological and the existing `while (output.length > rows - 1) output.pop()` backstop applies).
- **Scope creep:** A richer fix could elide individual status segments (e.g. hide `[auto-refresh on]` first, then downtime) instead of raw truncation — explicitly out of scope for this bug; file as a follow-up enhancement if desired.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When you say 'the info line at the top,' are you referring to the metadata table (Status, Priority, Stage, etc.) that sits below the pinned header in the detail view?" — Answer (user): "I mean the very first line, it contains the Work Items count, the auto-refresh status, the downtime status." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 1, Q1. Research: inspected `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `createListRenderer` header assembly (lines 3217–3229); top line is `Work Items — N item(s) [auto-refresh on] [Downtime …]` plus optional filter/paused segments.
- Q: "Should the fix pin the metadata table as well (so only the description/document viewer scrolls), or is there a different line/section you have in mind?" — Answer (user): "No." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 1, Q2.
- Q: "How many items should be in scope — just the metadata table in the detail view, or also the list-mode metadata panel at the bottom of the pane?" — Answer (user): "It has nothing to do with the meta-data (see 1)." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 1, Q3. Research: confirmed the issue is the list-mode header, not any metadata panel/table; detail view already has a pinned header+ToC via WL-0MSI28AP80002F5S.
- Q: "When this happens, is it the main list header (`Work Items — N item(s)...`) or a different line? And does it happen during normal list mode, or specifically when you're in the detail view for an item?" — Answer (user): "4 main" (i.e. the main list header). Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 2, Q4. Research: `createListRenderer` list-mode branch pushes `header` as `output[0]`; detail-mode path returns via `formatDetailView` and never renders the `Work Items` header.
- Q: "Does it happen with narrow terminal windows (e.g., 80 cols), or also at wider widths?" — Answer (user): "5. Narrow." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 2, Q5. Research: wide pans (253 cols) have ample space for the header; narrow panes (40–80 cols) reproduce the wrap — banners and long filter labels exacerbate it.
- Q: "Does the downtime status text include a timestamp that grows as time passes (e.g., `[downtime idle m:ss]`) — could this growing timestamp eventually cause the header line to wrap?" — Answer (user): "6. no - happens event when it says `[Downtime Off]`." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 2, Q6. Research: `renderDowntimeStatus` (worklist.ts:3077) returns `. [Downtime Off]` (shortest variant) when the worker is disabled — wrap reproduces even with this minimal segment, confirming the bug is not timer-growth-specific; discovered a typo in the answer ("event" = "even") and did not alter the captured intent.

# Audit Persist E2BIG — Code-Quality Findings Overflow

**Problem statement:** When the audit's code-quality scan produces a large number of findings (particularly bogus ruff parse errors on non-Python files), the assembled audit report exceeds the Linux 128 KB `argv` limit, causing `persist_audit.py` to crash with `OSError [Errno 7] E2BIG` — the audit verdict is never persisted.

**Users:**

- *Audit operator* (Pi agent): When they run `/skill:audit`, they expect a clean persist of the audit verdict. E2BIG failure blocks the workflow and requires manual intervention.
- *Herdr downtime worker*: Automated audits run by herdr fail silently when persist crashes, leaving items without audit records.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. **Per-linter file filtering** — Each linter must scope its input files to its native extensions (e.g. ruff → `.py/.pyi/.pyx` only; eslint → `.ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx`; shellcheck → `.sh/.bash/.zsh/.ksh`). Non-matching files must never be passed to the wrong linter.

2. **Report finding cap** — The audit report must cap the number of code-quality findings listed in the report table (e.g. show top 50 findings, then a summary line with "X additional findings"). Total findings count must still be accurate.

3. **File-based persist for large reports** — When the report text exceeds a threshold (e.g. 64 KB), `persist_audit.py` must use the file-based path (`--audit-file`) instead of `--raw-output` to avoid E2BIG.

4. **All existing audit behaviour preserved** — The fix must not change the audit verdict logic, false-positive screen, remediation loop, or any other audit pipeline step. Only the finding filtering, report rendering, and persist mechanism are affected.

5. **Regression tests** — New unit tests must cover: (a) ruff invoked with mixed file list receives only `.py` files; (b) report with 1000+ findings caps to N entries in the rendered table; (c) report >64 KB uses file-based persist.

**Constraints:**

- No breaking changes to the audit API or report schema.
- Must not introduce additional subprocess calls or external dependencies.
- Must work within the existing audit pipeline (no restructuring).
- Must pass the full project test suite.

**Existing state:**

- `_run_ruff_check` in `linter_runner.py` does filter to Python extensions, but may not cover all code paths (e.g. `run_ruff` public API, fix mode).
- The report table in `_assemble_issue_report` (`audit_runner.py`) iterates ALL findings with no cap.
- `persist_audit.py` passes the report as `--raw-output <text>` which hits E2BIG for large reports.
- A workaround exists: `--audit-file` flag on `wl audit-set` for file-based input.

**Desired change:**

1. Harden per-linter file filtering so every linter only receives files of its native extension.
2. Cap the findings table in the report to a configurable number (e.g. 50) with a summary line.
3. Add a threshold check in `persist_audit.py`: when report > 64 KB, write to a temp file and use `--audit-file` instead of `--raw-output`.

**Key Files (predicted):**

- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — Add threshold check and file-based persist path
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Cap findings in `_assemble_issue_report`
- `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — Harden per-linter file filtering

**Related work:**

- WL-0MSRG481O007QVEA — Discovered from (parent work item)
- WL-0MRSGMTYU009OZCF — Add --audit-file to wl audit-set for file-based audit input (the workaround)

**Risks & assumptions:**

- Risk: Adding file-based persist requires temp file cleanup; if the process is killed mid-write, orphaned temp files may accumulate. Mitigation: use `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=True)` which auto-deletes on close.
- Assumption: The 64 KB threshold is safe — well below the Linux 128 KB argv limit.
- Scope-creep risk: Do NOT add support for new linters beyond the existing set (ruff, eslint, markdownlint, shellcheck, dotnet-format). That is a separate feature.
- Assumption: The ruff file-filtering bug exists in at least one code path; if the filtering is already correct, the cap and file-based persist are still valuable as defense-in-depth.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: What is the maximum number of bogus findings that triggered E2BIG?
  A: Unknown — the work item describes "hundreds of bogus parse-error findings" from ruff on non-Python files. This should be measured as part of implementation. Source: work item description.

- Q: Should the report cap be configurable?
  A: Default to 50 findings in the table, with a configurable constant at the top of `audit_runner.py`. Source: agent recommendation based on standard report size budgets.

- Q: What threshold should trigger file-based persist?
  A: 64 KB — well below the 128 KB argv limit but large enough to avoid thrashing. Source: agent recommendation.
data.title: audit persist fails with E2BIG when code-quality scan lints non-Python files (ruff on .sh/.ts)

# Write unit tests for auto-downgrade of critical priority

## Goal
Add comprehensive unit tests covering the auto-downgrade behavior for critical priority items transitioning to terminal states.

## Test Coverage Required

Per Acceptance Criteria 4 of parent (WL-0MSJM4EIV001A0V9):

1. **`wl update --status completed`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high
2. **`wl update --stage in_review`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high

5. **No-op: non-terminal transitions** — verify critical priority unchanged when moving between non-terminal stages (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`)

- Tests should use the existing test infrastructure (see `tests/database.test.ts` and `tests/cli/`)
- Follow the existing test patterns for `cascadePriorityDowngrade` tests
- Tests should verify both the priority change AND the reporting output (AC3 of parent)
- Consider both JSON and human-readable output paths

- `tests/database.test.ts` — database layer tests
- `tests/cli/` — CLI command tests (update, close)

# Support multiple create options

Currently there is only a single create option in the Herdr plugin. Press `c` to create. Change this into a chord that allows different create options.

## Create Options

### c-n (create intake)
- Existing behaviour preserved
- Runs: `/intake <description> --priority <priority default='medium'>`

### c-q (create quick)
- New quick-create form with fields: title, description, priority
- Runs: `wl create -t '<title>' -d '<description>' -p '<priority>'`
- Reuses the existing form-dialog system from `form-dialog.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Single-key `c` shortcut removed from shortcuts.json
2. `c-n` chord triggers the existing intake flow (description + priority form, feeds to LLM)
3. `c-q` chord triggers a quick-create flow with three fields: title, description, priority
4. Quick create form runs `wl create` with title, description, and priority values from the form
5. Both chords are visible in the shortcuts help panel
6. All existing shortcuts continue to work unchanged

## Implementation Notes

- The shortcut system (`shortcut-config.ts`) already supports chords of any length
- The form-dialog system (`form-dialog.ts`) can be reused for both create forms
- The existing `c` shortcut entry in `shortcuts.json` should be replaced with two entries: `["c", "n"]` and `["c", "q"]`

## Goal

Wire the hydrator into the worklist plugin (packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts) as a TaskScheduler task, visibility-gated, with an immediate run when the tab regains focus (reusing the existing resume-poll machinery). No second interval loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A scheduler task id 'hydrate' is registered on the existing TaskScheduler with intervalMs 30_000, singleFlight: true, and runTimeoutMs set; a rejecting task never takes down the scheduler loop.
2. The hydrate task is visibility-gated: while the worklist pane is hidden it does not run and spawns zero wl processes (paneGate pattern).
3. On a hidden→visible transition, hydration runs immediately (in addition to the existing refresh) without waiting for the next 30s tick.
4. Hydrator deps are injected into worklist.ts (e.g. via opts) so tests can substitute fakes.
5. Full project suite passes; no regressions in existing worklist tests.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts — register hydrate task + resume hook
- packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts — reused as-is
- packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts — reuse PollGate/paneGate
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts — visibility-gated scheduler precedent

## Minimal Implementation

1. Register hydrate task alongside refresh/sync/resume-poll/downtime with the same interval/visibility wiring used by the downtime worker.
2. In the resume-poll hidden→visible transition branch, invoke the hydrate task immediately (parallel to the existing immediate refresh).

## Dependencies

- Requires F2 (hydrator module — runHydrationOnce to invoke)

## Goal

Implement the herdr hydrator module (packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts): every 30s (and on worklist focus-resume) it fetches all in_progress work items, matches each against work-item IDs in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace, and demotes any item with no matching pane per the signal-based rule (AC3 of parent WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI). Pure decision functions + orchestration with injectable deps; fail-open at every boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes) returns WL-[0-9A-Z]+ IDs found in pane labels.
2. isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes) returns true iff the ID appears in a running pane's label in any tab of the current workspace; workspace filtering via herdr pane list --workspace <id> / HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID env var.
3. decideDemotion(workItem, blockers): stage in_review → {status: completed, stage: in_review}; active outbound blocker (target not completed/deleted, stage not in_review/done, per isDependencyActive in packages/shared/src/database.ts) → {status: blocked, stage: plan_complete (or best compatible)}; else → {status: open, stage: intake_complete}; stage always chosen per src/config.ts compatibility.
4. runHydrationOnce(deps): fetches wl list --status in_progress, fetches panes, computes demotions, applies each via wl update (status+stage); an item with a matching pane is never touched.
5. Fail-open: wl/pane CLI missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output → skip the entire cycle with a log; the function never throws; no demotion happens on untrustworthy evidence.
6. All hydrator.test.ts tests pass; full project suite passes.

## Key Files

# Intake Brief: Remove OpenBrain (WL-0MTH28WDS008WMXA)

## Problem statement

OpenBrain is an optional integration (`src/openbrain.ts`) that spawns the `ob` CLI to submit a summary whenever a work item is marked completed. This project enabled it for local testing (`openBrainEnabled: true` in `.worklog/config.yaml`, commit `66fb51a8`) but the `ob` binary is not installed, so every `wl update`/`wl close` that completes an item emits `[openbrain] ...` errors to stderr. The integration is unused and, per producer confirmation, is to be **removed entirely** — both from the shared codebase and from this project's config.

## Users

- **Developers** running `wl update`/`wl close` in this project — they see stray `[openbrain]` errors and want clean output.
- **Worklog maintainers** — they want dead integration code (which requires an `ob` binary nobody has and whose `wl openbrain` commands were never implemented) removed from the shared CLI.

User stories:
- As a developer in this project, I want `wl update` to complete a work item without emitting `[openbrain]` errors, so my terminal output is clean.
- As a Worklog maintainer, I want the OpenBrain integration absent from the shared codebase, so there is no dead code and no misleading docs/plugin references.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Feature removed from the shared codebase**: `src/openbrain.ts` deleted; `submitToOpenBrain` imports and call sites removed from `src/commands/update.ts` and `src/commands/close.ts`; `openBrainEnabled` removed from `WorklogConfig` in `packages/shared/src/types.ts`.
2. **Project-scoped disablement**: `openBrainEnabled: true` removed from `.worklog/config.yaml` in this repository.
3. **No dangling references or dead artifacts**: `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts`, `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts`, and `docs/openbrain.md` deleted; OpenBrain references removed from `CLI.md` and `README.md`. A repo-wide search (`rg -i "openbrain|submitToOpenBrain|openBrainEnabled"`) returns no matches in tracked source/docs (excluding git history and regenerated `dist/` artifacts).
4. **Error gone**: completing a work item via `wl update` and `wl close` in this project produces no `[openbrain]` stderr output (validated by the CLI test run, AC5).
5. **Green build & docs**: full project test suite passes with the new changes; all related documentation reflects the removal (README, CLI.md, code comments, docs table).

## Constraints

- No behavior changes beyond removing the OpenBrain path — `wl close`/`wl update` semantics (recursive close, re-sort, audit handling) are untouched.
- Worktrees under `.worklog/worktrees/*` are separate feature branches — do not edit them in this change; only the main checkout is in scope.
- Config user file `.worklog/config.yaml` is the only place `openBrainEnabled` is set in this repo; `config.defaults.yaml` does not set it (verify at implementation time).
- The optional retry-queue file `.worklog/openbrain-queue.jsonl` may exist from failed submissions; it is transient data, not code — no action required beyond optionally removing it.

## Existing state

- `src/openbrain.ts` implements `submitToOpenBrain()` (spawns `ob add --stdin --title …`), `buildOpenBrainSummary()`, `appendToQueue()` (retry queue), and `resolveObBinary()` (`WL_OB_BIN` or `ob`).
- `src/commands/update.ts`: calls `submitToOpenBrain(item)` when `updates.status === 'completed'` and `config.openBrainEnabled`.
- `src/commands/close.ts`: calls `submitToOpenBrain(updated)` from the force, audit-gated recursive, and standard close paths when `config.openBrainEnabled`; the recovery path comments reference OpenBrain.
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts`: `WorklogConfig` declares `openBrainEnabled?: boolean`.
- `.worklog/config.yaml`: `openBrainEnabled: true`.
- Docs: `docs/openbrain.md`; `CLI.md` lists `wl openbrain status/resubmit` (commands were never implemented); `README.md` docs table links `docs/openbrain.md`.
- Tests: `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts`, `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts`.
- `ob` is not on PATH and `WL_OB_BIN` is unset; the globally installed `wl` (`/usr/local/bin/wl`) symlinks to this repo's built `dist/cli.js`, so a rebuild is required to actually stop the errors.

## Desired change

Remove the OpenBrain integration and its project config toggle:

- Delete `src/openbrain.ts`, `docs/openbrain.md`, `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts`, `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts`.
- In `src/commands/update.ts` / `src/commands/close.ts`: drop the `submitToOpenBrain` import and every `openBrainEnabled` fire-and-forget block (including the recovery-path comment).
- In `packages/shared/src/types.ts`: remove `openBrainEnabled?: boolean`.
- In `.worklog/config.yaml`: remove `openBrainEnabled: true`.
- In `CLI.md` / `README.md`: remove OpenBrain references.
- Rebuild (`npm run build:shared && npm run build`) so the installed `wl` no longer ships `openbrain.js` in `dist/`.

## Key Files:

- `src/openbrain.ts` — delete (entire module)
- `src/commands/update.ts` — remove import + completion call block
- `src/commands/close.ts` — remove import + three close-path call blocks + recovery comment
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` — remove `openBrainEnabled` from `WorklogConfig`
- `.worklog/config.yaml` — remove `openBrainEnabled: true`
- `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts` — delete
- `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts` — delete
- `docs/openbrain.md` — delete
- `docs/feature-requests/openbrain-playwright-fallback-retrieval.md` — delete (OpenBrain feature request; would fail AC3 repo-wide search)
- `CLI.md`, `README.md` — remove OpenBrain references

## Related work

- WL-0MNM4SDMA000GOBC — "Whenever a work item is marked as completed/done update OpenBrain": introduced the integration (predecessor).
- WL-0MOHP1FIP007LYCB — "Make wl close OpenBrain submission fully non-blocking": changed the close flow (predecessor).
- WL-0MNRPS89H004COB0 — "Fix validator and openbrain test failures": fixed CLI.md docs + EPIPE handling (predecessor).
- WL-0MRTSOK8C009CDLA — "Process lifecycle utility module": references `src/openbrain.ts` as a spawn user; the process-lifecycle/spawn helpers themselves must be preserved.
- WL-0MQP4RDG2006LFM9 — ruff lint fix whose description matched `docs/openbrain.md` (search-index noise only).

## Effort and Risk

- Effort: **S** — deletions plus a handful of targeted edits; rebuild required.
- Risk: **Low** — opt-in flag; no other project enables it; `ob` unavailable so no live dependents. Residual risks: missed references (mitigated by the AC3 repo-wide search) and stale built `dist/` (mitigated by the rebuild in Desired change / AC5).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1** (Map/intake, 2026-09-19): "Should 'Remove openbrain' mean (A) remove the integration from the shared `worklog` codebase (~600 lines), or (B) only disable it in this project's `.worklog/config.yaml` (one line)? The title points at (A), the description ('in this project, but not any other … disable it') at (B). Reply A, B, or both."
  - **Answer (producer): "Both"** — do (A) **and** (B): remove the feature from the shared codebase AND remove the `openBrainEnabled: true` line from `.worklog/config.yaml`. Source: producer reply to comment WL-C0MU89PEMR004ISDS on WL-0MTH28WDS008WMXA.

# Pawn shop should reduce, not increase reputation (WL-0MTH6B20C002ZOM2) — Intake brief

## Problem statement

The Pawn Shop business card (`biz-pawnshop`, Main Street game, `Tableau-Card-Engine`) is currently **increasing** the player's reputation by +5 per turn and costs 300 coins to purchase — both incorrect per design intent. A pawn shop should be a low-reputation, budget-friendly establishment: it should **reduce** reputation by 0.1 per turn and be cheaper to acquire (200 coins at the ×100 scale, i.e. 2.00 in game terms).

## Users (example user stories)

- **As a player**, I expect placing a Pawn Shop on my street to slightly harm my reputation each turn (`-0.1`), not boost it, so that reputation decisions involve meaningful trade-offs.
- **As a player**, I expect the Pawn Shop to remain an accessible budget business (cheaper than the 300-coin tier-2 group) despite its per-turn reputation penalty.
- **As a maintainer**, I expect CSV card data and tests to stay internally consistent (numeric columns valid; ongoing-cost convention preserved).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Negative reputation per turn.** `biz-pawnshop.reputationPerTurn` in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` changes from `5` to `-0.1`; placing the Pawn Shop on the street grid accrues a **negative** reputation delta (−0.1) during the income phase (`applyIncome`), never a positive one.
2. **Reduced purchase cost.** `biz-pawnshop.cost` in the CSV changes from `300` to `200`; the market purchase price for the Pawn Shop is 200 (2.00 at the ×100 display convention).
3. **Synergy opt-out unchanged.** The Pawn Shop still provides and receives **zero** synergy bonuses (`synergyCoinBonus = 0`, `synergyRepBonus = 0`, no adjacency synergy) — unchanged behaviour (existing tests in `adjacency.test.ts` / `MainStreetHandSynergy.test.ts` still pass).
4. **Test coverage.** Add or extend automated tests asserting (a) the Pawn Shop's negative per-turn reputation and (b) its updated cost of 200; the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
5. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (card tooltips/descriptions generated from CSV, `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` and any README/wikis as applicable, including code comments). Note: `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- CSV numeric columns are validated by `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` (`parseFloat`); `-0.1` is a valid numeric value.
- Costs use the ×100 integer convention (200 = 2.00 coins); `reputationPerTurn` is applied raw at income time (no ×100) — confirm via tests during implementation.
- **Do not** regenerate costs via the balance-cards curve tool (`src/balance-cards/algorithm.ts`): it would reassign tier bands. Its Pawn Shop special case (cost −2) applies only when `baseIncome === 0`, which is not our case — no algorithm change needed.
- Ongoing-cost convention (documented in `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts`) is `max(25, cost / 4)`. **Assumption (producer to confirm):** if `cost` becomes 200, `ongoingCost` follows the convention to 50 (currently 75). The producer's clarification specified only the purchase cost; do not change `ongoingCost` unless confirmed.

## Existing state

Current `biz-pawnshop` row in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`:

```
business,biz-pawnshop,Pawn Shop,300,230,Commerce,...,1,5,0,0,Trades second-hand goods. Does not provide or receive synergy bonuses.,2,...,75,...
```

- `cost = 300`, `baseIncome = 230`, `reputationPerTurn = 5`, `synergyCoinBonus = 0`, `synergyRepBonus = 0`, `tier = 2`, `ongoingCost = 75`.
- The Pawn Shop currently **adds** 5 reputation per turn (raw ledger units) and costs 3.00 coins (×100: 300).
- All six tier-2 businesses share `cost 300 / income 230 / rep 5 / ongoingCost 75`; changing only the Pawn Shop is a deliberate divergence.

## Desired change

| Field | Current | Desired |
|---|---|---|
| `reputationPerTurn` | `5` | `-0.1` (reduces reputation 0.1/turn) |
| `cost` | `300` | `200` (2.00 at ×100) |
| `ongoingCost` | `75` | `50` — **assumption**, follows `cost/4` convention; pending confirmation |
| `synergyCoinBonus` / `synergyRepBonus` / `tier` / `baseIncome` | `0` / `0` / `2` / `230` | unchanged |

## Risks & assumptions

- **Ongoing-cost convention (assumption, unconfirmed).** Changing `cost` to 200 implies `ongoingCost = 50` per the documented `max(25, cost/4)` convention; the producer's clarification only covered the purchase cost. Implementer should confirm before touching `ongoingCost`; leaving it at 75 leaves a convention inconsistency (risk: low).
- **Unit conventions.** Costs are ×100 integers; `reputationPerTurn` is applied raw. If the game's ×100 scaling applies to reputation in the current branch, `-0.1` may need to be stored as `-10` — validate against the repo's existing tests before finalising the CSV value (risk: medium; mitigated by AC1's negative-delta assertion).
- **Do not regenerate balances.** Running the balance-cards tool would reassign the Pawn Shop's tier band and overwrite the manual cost; the change is a data-only edit plus tests.
- **Scope-creep guard.** The Pawn Shop's card *description* text could mention its reputation penalty, but that is an extra opportunity — record as a linked work item if desired, not part of this item's scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Pawn Shop row: `reputationPerTurn`, `cost` (and `ongoingCost` per assumption)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — template loading from CSV (read-only; verifies `-0.1` and `200` parse)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — `applyIncome` reputation accrual loop (read-only; confirms negative deltas apply)
- `tests/main-street/…` — new/extended tests (e.g. alongside `business-ongoing-cost.test.ts` / `turn-cash-net.test.ts`) for negative rep/turn and cost 200
- `src/balance-cards/algorithm.ts` — no change expected (verify special case is unaffected)
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — update if the Pawn Shop row description changes

## Related work

- `WL-0MTCMVIPS007AB02` — "End of game stats" (open; text-overlap match only, no dependency).
- `WL-0MSGTSPXK007POB1`, `WL-0MT1KJNHE0048HW3` — text-overlap matches from the automated report; not related.
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — documents the Pawn Shop no-synergy special case.
- Existing Pawn Shop synergy opt-out tests: `tests/main-street/adjacency.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/same-type-synergy.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/synergy-visuals.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/MainStreetHandSynergy.test.ts` (all covered by AC3).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

1. **Q:** "The description says 'Reduce the cost of the pawn shop to 2' — which field should be changed? `cost` (purchase price, currently 300) → reduce to 2? `ongoingCost` (per-turn operating cost, currently 75) → reduce to 2? Or some other cost field? The reputation change (from +5 to −0.1 per turn) is clear."
   **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "Neither should be reduced to 2. This is from when costs were lower, now it should be 200."
   **Final accepted answer:** the **`cost`** field changes `300 → 200` (×100 scale; 2.00 in game terms). The original "to 2" wording was from an earlier lower-cost economy and is superseded.
   Research summary: inspected `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` (pawn shop row), `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` (numeric validation), `MainStreetCards.ts` (template loading), `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` (`applyIncome` reputation accrual), `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts` (ongoing-cost convention `max(25, cost/4)`), and `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md`.

### Related work items

- **WL-0MT1KJNHE0048HW3** – snapd udev monitor goroutine hang - watchdog kills and restart loops (completed)

# Dispatch-logs Skill: Generate Global Dispatch Reports

A `/skill:dispatch-logs` command that produces a concise, human-readable (or JSON) 24-hour dispatch activity report across all projects on the machine — including leader state, timeline, errors, and coordination status — with support for custom time windows and per-project filtering.

## Problem Statement

Operators investigating overnight dispatches must manually aggregate `*/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` files across all projects on the machine. There is no single command to produce a concise 24-hour (or custom window) global dispatch report.

## Users

- **Operator on-call**: Needs a quick view of what dispatches ran overnight and whether any errors occurred.
- **Debugging engineer**: Tracing a specific dispatch failure across projects.
- **Team lead**: Reviewing dispatch activity trends over a custom time window.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `/skill:dispatch-logs` produces a human-readable report covering all projects on the machine for the last 24 hours (default window).
2. All invocation flags work correctly: `--hours N`, `--since`/`--until` ISO timestamps, `--project <name>`, and `--json` for machine-readable output.
3. The report includes five sections: (a) leader summary, (b) dispatch timeline, (c) error summary, (d) coordination state, and (e) known issues.
4. Gracefully handles the case when no dispatch logs exist (produces an empty/clean report, not an error).
5. Unit tests pass for log parsing, argument handling, and report structure (using mocked log files).
6. SKILL.md is complete with name, description, invocation examples, and frontmatter.

## Constraints

- Log files are in JSONL format (one JSON object per line).
- Machine coordination state lives in `~/.herdr/downtime/` (two JSON files).
- Must skip `node_modules`, `dist`, `build` directories during project root discovery.
- Default window is 24 hours from `Date.now()`; custom windows use ISO 8601 timestamps.

## Existing State

- Per-worklog dispatch logs exist at `*/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.
- Machine-wide coordination at `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` and `downtime-leader-lease.json`.

Create a new skill in `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/` with:

# Intake Brief — Smart Audit Re-instatement

**Headline:** When the audit freshness check (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`) flags an audit as stale, the system should automatically review the changes made since the audit and decide whether to re-instate the original audit or flag the item for re-audit — rather than treating all post-audit changes as requiring a full re-run.

## Problem statement

Audits are invalidated whenever a work item's `updatedAt` changes after the audit time (`isAuditNotReadyFresh` checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt`). However, many changes do not affect the code or implementation that was audited (e.g., changing a comment, updating assignee). The audit skill should automatically inspect the changes since the audit and decide whether to re-instate the original audit or require a new one.

**Producer clarification:** The system should inspect anything that changes the intent of the work item or actions taken against it — description, comments, audit text, dependencies, commit messages.

## Users

- **Developers using `wl next` / Pi TUI:** Audited items should not be unnecessarily re-audited when changes are irrelevant to the implementation.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher:** Should not re-dispatch items that were recently audited and whose changes are non-semantic.
- **Producers:** A "Ready to close: Yes" item should stay ready unless changes actually affect the audit outcome.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Automatic re-instatement detection:** When `isAuditNotReadyFresh` returns `false` (audit flagged as stale), the system automatically inspects the changes made since `auditedAt` and decides whether to re-instate the audit or flag for re-audit.
2. **Change inspection covers key fields:** The inspection examines description, comments, audit text, dependencies, and commit messages for changes that could affect the audit outcome. Non-semantic changes (e.g., metadata-only updates) do not trigger re-audit.
3. **Re-instatement logic:** If changes are deemed non-semantic (no impact on audit outcome), the original audit is re-instated by resetting `updatedAt` to `auditedAt` (same pattern as `saveAuditResult`). If changes are semantic, the audit is flagged as needing re-run.
4. **Full project test suite passes** with new regression tests covering re-instatement of non-semantic changes and re-audit flag for semantic changes.

- Change confined to audit freshness logic in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and the audit result management in the persistent store.

- Must preserve existing audit behavior for items with no previous audit.
- Must be fully automatic — no operator intervention required.

- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:1038`** — `saveAuditResult` resets `updatedAt = auditedAt` to keep audits fresh after audit writes.
- **`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`** — Audit results stored in SQLite; `getAllAuditResults` / `saveAuditResult` methods.

## Desired change

1. Create a new function `assessAuditInvalidate(changesSinceAudited, auditResult)` that inspects the delta between the audit time and current state.
2. The function should classify changes as semantic (affect audit outcome) or non-semantic (no impact).
3. For non-semantic changes, re-instate the audit (reset `updatedAt = auditedAt`).
4. For semantic changes, mark the audit as needing re-run.
5. Integrate into the `wl next` / TUI flow where audit freshness is checked.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` (line 644), audit map builder, sorting logic
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — Audit storage methods, `batchUpdateSortIndices` (line 747-769)
- `packages/shared/src/sync.ts` — Sync merge logic

- **Semantic boundary ambiguity:** What counts as a semantic change is subjective. **Assumption:** Changes to description, comments, dependencies, and commit messages are semantic; changes to assignee, tags, priority, and sortIndex are non-semantic. Document the rule in code comments.
- **Scope creep:** Requests for configurable invalidation policies. **Mitigation:** Keep this to the concrete scenarios identified; file separate items for broader policy changes.

# Log all dispatches and auto close all completed dispatch panes, except implement

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher creates panes for each work item it dispatches (intake, plan, audit, risk-effort), but panes stay open indefinitely until an operator closes them manually. There is no automatic pane lifecycle management — completed panes clutter the Dispatcher workspace and the dispatch log lacks pane-close status updates (intake complete, plan complete, audit passed/failed, or stuck). This work item adds automatic pane closing and enhanced logging for pane lifecycle events.

## Users

- **Operator** — wants the Dispatcher workspace to stay tidy; auto-closed panes reduce manual cleanup.
- **Producer** — wants a clear audit trail of pane outcomes in the dispatch log: which panes completed successfully, which are stuck, and which failed their audit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** The downtime worker logs every pane-close event to `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` with: ISO timestamp, work item ID, work item title, pane ID, dispatch kind (`plan`/`intake`/`audit`/`risk-effort`), and outcome (`closed-as-intake-complete`, `closed-as-plan-complete`, `audit-passed`, `audit-failed`, `requires-attention`).
- **AC2:** When a dispatched item's stage advances to `intake_complete` or `plan_complete`, the worker records the appropriate log entry and closes the associated pane (except for `kind === 'implement'` items).
- **AC3:** When a dispatched item is left in any other state (e.g. `in_review` without reaching a terminal state, or blocked by producer questions where `needsProducerReview === true`), the worker records a `requires-attention` log entry with a summary reason.
- **AC4:** When a dispatched item reaches `in_review` status (implementation completed), the worker records the event in the log.
- **AC5:** When an audit pane completes and the item's audit status is recorded (`auditedAt` set, audit passed or failed), the worker records the audit outcome in the log and closes the pane (audit panes are always auto-closed regardless of the `implement` exception).
- **AC6:** The `implement` kind is EXCLUDED from all auto-close logic — implement panes remain open until manually closed by the operator.
- **AC7:** All logging and pane-closing operations are fail-closed: a failed log write or pane-close attempt must never crash the worker or block subsequent dispatches.
- **AC8:** Full herdr + repo test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The existing `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` rolling JSONL format must be extended (not replaced); legacy entries remain valid.
- Pane closing must be safe — only panes that were spawned by the downtime worker for this specific work item should be closed.
- The worker must detect state changes without polling the worklog excessively; consider event-driven or reasonable polling cadence.
- The `implements` exception (AC6) is mandatory — no implement pane is ever auto-closed.

## Existing state

- Dispatch logging already exists via `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8): a bounded JSONL log recording dispatched items.
- The `AgentTracker` (`agent-tracker.ts`) already records work-item → pane-ID associations in `.worklog/agent-panes.json`.
- Panes are spawned via `send-to-pi.sh` with pane IDs that are captured and tracked.
- Panes currently stay open indefinitely — no auto-close mechanism exists.
- The worker polls `wl` commands periodically but does not track work-item state changes post-dispatch.

## Desired change

1. **Extend the dispatch log schema** to support pane-close and state-change entries with outcome reasons.
2. **Add a pane-lifecycle monitor** that tracks dispatched items after they are spawned, detecting when they reach terminal stages (`intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `in_review`) or when audits complete.
3. **Implement auto-close logic** that closes panes based on the detected outcome, with the `implement` exception.
4. **Log all lifecycle events** to the dispatch log with structured entries.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Core dispatch worker; add pane-lifecycle tracking and auto-close logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — Extend log entry schema for pane-close outcomes.
- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.ts` — Already tracks pane IDs; may need extension for lifecycle callbacks.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — New tests for pane-close logic.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8** — *Log herdr downtime dispatches (item comment + rolling .worklog log)* — existing dispatch logging infrastructure.
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** — *Work-item ↔ agent-pane association tracker* — `AgentTracker` that maps work items to pane IDs.
- **WL-0MU2EP6JL006A1U3** — *Remove client-side pane count cap* — panes now deliberately stay open until manually closed (context for why auto-close is new).
- **WL-0MTJQOZ0K007KD40** — *Dispatch-logs skill: generates 24h global dispatch report* — related observability.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should happen to panes for items that reach `in_review` but then revert to a different stage?" — Answer: Log the initial `in_review` arrival; if the pane is still open and the item changes again, log the new state. Only close panes at the specific terminal points defined in AC2–AC5. Source: intake draft.
- Q: "Does 'requires attention' apply to panes that are still actively running (agent in `working` state)?" — Answer: No — "requires attention" applies to panes where the agent session has ended (`done` state) but the work item has not reached a terminal stage (`intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `in_review`). Source: intake draft.
- Q: "Should the worker proactively close panes, or just log and signal?" — Answer: The worker should both log AND close the pane (except for implement). The pane close is an active action. Source: intake draft.

# Intake Brief: Fix mode-switch flip-flop — leader election for proxy mode changes

## Problem statement

When multiple herdr panes are open, each creates an independent `ModeSwitchWorker` with its own idle clock. Active and idle panes fight over the same proxy — the active pane's fast flips are immediately undone by idle panes' cheap flips, causing a rapid flip-flop pattern (13–20 second cycles) in logs.

## Users

- **Primary:** Operator using herdr with multiple panes — experiences unreliable proxy mode switching due to flip-flopping.
- **Secondary:** herdr developers debugging proxy mode behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Leader-only mode switching:** Only the downtime leader performs mode switches (cheap POST). Non-leader instances skip `tick()` cheap-switch logic entirely.
2. **Shared activity broadcast:** All instances read/write a shared `mode-activity.json` file in the coordination directory. Any instance receiving a command broadcasts; all instances use the shared timestamp. Proxy stays fast while *any* pane has recent activity.
3. **60-minute idle threshold:** `DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` changed from 900,000 ms (15 min) to 3,600,000 ms (60 min). A clamped-settings test verifies the new default.
4. **No flip-flopping:** With two panes open (one active, one idle), the proxy remains in fast mode while the active pane receives commands, regardless of the idle pane's local clock.
5. **Graceful leader transitions:** On leadership change, the new leader reads the shared activity file and continues from correct state — no spurious mode changes during election.
6. **Fail-closed on broadcast failure:** If shared activity state cannot be read/written, the instance falls back to its local clock (safe: stays fast longer rather than risking premature cheap switch).
7. **Full test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- Must reuse the existing downtime leader (`DowntimeWorker.isLeader`), not create a separate leader election.
- Shared activity file lives in the coordination directory (`~/.herdr/downtime/` or `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` override).
- Fail-closed: if coordination fails, the instance must not prematurely switch to cheap mode.
- All related work (leader election, downtime dispatcher, mode-switch idle trigger) is already completed.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts:319` — `lastOperatorCommandAt` tracked per-instance, no inter-instance coordination.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1401` — `createModeSwitchWorker()` called once per pane, before `createDowntimeWorker()`.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts:125` — `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs: 900_000` (15 min).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:3951` — `DowntimeWorker.isLeader` exists as a readonly boolean.

## Desired change

1. Wire `downtimeWorker.isLeader` into `ModeSwitchWorker` via `createModeSwitchWorker()` constructor options.
2. Add shared activity file read/write in the coordination directory (`mode-activity.json`).
3. `tick()`: non-leaders return immediately; leaders evaluate and fire cheap POST.
4. `onOperatorCommand()`: all instances update shared activity; only leader fires fast POST.
5. On `tick()`, both leaders and non-leaders read shared activity file for unified idle evaluation.
6. Change default idle threshold from 15 min to 60 min.
7. Add comprehensive tests.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` — leader-gated `tick()` and `onOperatorCommand()`; shared activity broadcast/read
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — change `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` default from 900_000 to 3_600_000
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — pass `downtimeWorker.isLeader` and `coordinationDir` into the mode-switch worker (may need to reorder creation to happen after `createDowntimeWorker()`)
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` — new tests for leader-gating, shared activity broadcast, no flip-flop, graceful leader transitions
- README — document the 60-minute default, leader-gating, and shared activity broadcast

## Risks & Assumptions

1. **Leader election overlap during transitions:** Brief dual-leadership during lease handoff could cause double mode switches. Mitigation: `tick()` is already single-flighted (`switchInFlight` guard); a double switch would resolve to the correct state on the next poll.
2. **Coordination directory existence:** The shared activity file requires the coordination directory to exist. Assumption: `createDowntimeWorker` already ensures directory creation (confirmed via existing `getMachineCoordinationDir()` usage).
3. **Concurrent file writes:** Multiple instances writing `mode-activity.json` simultaneously. Mitigation: use atomic writes (write to temp file, then rename) or rely on small synchronous writes that are atomic at the OS level for small JSON objects.
4. **Reordering `createModeSwitchWorker`:** In `index.ts`, the mode-switch worker is currently created *before* the downtime worker so it can accept the `onProxyIdle` callback. Passing `isLeader` requires creating the downtime worker first. Mitigation: the callback can be wired after both workers exist — no ordering change needed for the callback itself.
5. **Scope creep:** This fix is scoped to leader-gating and shared activity. Do not add new coordination protocols, gossip, or network-based mechanisms.

## Related work

- **WL-0MTF0KLO10043YAN** — Single machine-wide downtime leader across all worklogs (completed, done)
- **WL-0MSXH3UF5000HJUS** — Implement leader election module with 5-minute lease management (completed, done)
- **WL-0MU4MKVR4005WPBJ** — Herdr mode-switch worker: modeSwitchEnabled defaults to false (completed, in_review)
- **WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9** — Herdr plugin: activity-gated proxy mode switching (completed, done)

- Q: None — the work item was sufficiently defined to proceed without clarification.

`dispatchFromHerdrList` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) builds the

flagged for review.

# RCA: downtime dispatcher sends nothing in cheap mode despite 2–3 idle slots

## Symptom

In cheap mode the local llama-proxy reports 3 slots with 2–3 idle for extended periods, yet the
herdr downtime dispatcher produces no dispatches. Observed in the window immediately before the
proxy was switched to fast mode (2026-09-19 ~00:13Z).

## Evidence (llama-proxy status log, proxy clock = UTC+1)

Source: `GET http://192.168.0.199:8000/logs/tail?source=proxy&lines=100000` (log file starts at
proxy 00:00 = UTC 23:00 on 2026-09-18).

- Window proxy 01:01–01:12 = **UTC 00:01–00:12**: `mode=cheap`, `total_slots=3`,
  `available_slots=2` (constant — 2 slots idle), and **zero** dispatches in
  `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.
- `local_owner_session_id = ["http://localhost:8080","herdr-1789775322-722064-10708"]` — the owner
  is a **dispatched downtime pane** (`Downtime triggered implement … CG-0MTIOLY2A0092OT1`), whose
  local dispatch lease ran 836s → 0 across the window (`local_active_query=true` throughout).
- Across the whole UTC 23:00–04:11 log: **56%** of status samples had ≥2 idle slots **and** an
  active lease; **10%** had all slots idle **and** an active lease.

## Root cause

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `tick()`:

```ts
const ownerLeaseHeld = /* local_owner_session_id string OR local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds > 0 */;
const slotOwned = ownerLeaseHeld && (runningPanes ?? 0) > 0;
const contentionQueueDepth = ...;
if (slotOwned) return { polled: true, dispatched: false, idle: true };
if (contentionQueueDepth > 0) return { polled: true, dispatched: false, idle: true };
```

This gate runs **before** the coordination file is read, is **machine-wide**, and has **no per-slot
branch** — it fires even in per-slot mode (`requiredFreeSlots=1 < total=3`). While any dispatched
agent is alive and holds the shared local-dispatch lease, the dispatcher refuses to dispatch at
all, leaving the remaining unowned free slots unused. In cheap mode a single long-running agent
therefore monopolises the dispatcher's permission for the whole generation (adaptive lease up to
`local_dispatch_lease_max_seconds`, default 1500s; observed 840s).

The code comment claims the gate is only a single-slot (count-based) fallback superseded by per-slot
identity, and that leases expire in ~180s. Both assumptions are false for this deployment.

## Contributing causes

1. **Owner-signal schema drift** — the proxy serves `local_owner_session_id` as a JSON **array**;
   `parseLlamaStatus` expects a **string** and silently drops it, so the worker cannot identify the
   owning slot/session and falls back to `lease_remaining > 0`.
2. **No queue-depth signal** — `contention_queue_depth` is not served in this configuration.
3. **Header vs proxy UI disagree** — the herdr header only shows idle when *all* slots are idle,
   while the proxy UI shows `available_slots`; "idle slots but no dispatches" is invisible in herdr.
4. **Scheduler targets the affected window** — the mode scheduler is `[('01:00','cheap'),('10:00','fast')]`,
   so the overnight window is precisely the one this gate wastes.

## Goal

Restore cheap-mode overnight throughput by removing the machine-wide dispatch block, aligning the
owner-lease contract, and making the gate decision observable.

## Acceptance criteria

1. In cheap mode with ≥1 unowned free slot, a dispatched agent holding a lease no longer prevents
   dispatch (measured: dispatches resume during agent runs).
2. The proxy owner-lease payload is parsed without silent data loss and covered by a contract test.
3. The dispatcher records *why* it did not dispatch (`slotOwned` / `contention` / `no-candidate` /
   `review-queue-hold` / `code-freeze`) to `downtime-coordination.log` and the header.
4. The lease-TTL assumption in `downtime-worker.ts` matches the proxy's adaptive-lease behaviour.

Children cover each fix; see the child items of this RCA.

# Make the downtime owner-lease gate per-slot

Parent RCA: WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28.

## Goal

In cheap mode (3 slots) the downtime dispatcher must keep dispatching into **unowned free slots**
even while another dispatched agent holds the shared local-dispatch lease. Today it dispatches
nothing for the whole duration of any agent run, wasting 2–3 slots.

## Problem

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `tick()` applies a **machine-wide** gate before reading the
coordination file:

```ts
const ownerLeaseHeld = /* local_owner_session_id string OR local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds > 0 */;
const slotOwned = ownerLeaseHeld && (runningPanes ?? 0) > 0;
if (slotOwned) return { polled: true, dispatched: false, idle: true };
```

There is no per-slot branch — it fires even when `requiredFreeSlots < total_slots` (per-slot mode).
So a single working agent that holds a lease blocks all dispatch, despite `countFreeUnownedSlots`
reporting free slots. Evidence: proxy UTC 00:01–00:12, cheap mode, `total_slots=3`,
`available_slots=2`, lease held by a dispatched pane, **zero dispatches**.

The gate's comment claims it is only the count-based (single-slot) fallback and is superseded by
per-slot identity. That is not what the code does.

## Required behaviour

- Detect per-slot mode from the status (`Array.isArray(status.slots)` and a usable slot array).
- In per-slot mode, allow dispatch while `countFreeUnownedSlots(status.slots) >= <tier minimum>`;
  the global owner lease must not block dispatch into free unowned slots.
- Keep the conservative gate only for the count-based (single-slot / no per-slot data) path, so a
  truly owned sole slot is still protected.
- Never dispatch into a slot whose per-slot `owner_session_id` is set.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Unit test: per-slot status with 3 slots, 1 owned/busy and 2 free unowned, a held global lease,
   and `runningPanes > 0` → dispatch **proceeds** (regression test for this RCA).

# parseLlamaStatus: accept the proxy's array local_owner_session_id (+ per-slot owner contract test)

Parent RCA: WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28.

## Goal

Stop silently dropping the proxy's local-owner signal so the dispatcher can reason about ownership
per slot instead of falling back to `lease_remaining > 0`.

## Problem

The llama-proxy now serves `local_owner_session_id` as a JSON **array**, e.g.:

```json
"local_owner_session_id": ["http://localhost:8080", "herdr-1789775322-722064-10708"],
"local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds": 29.99
```

`parseLlamaStatus` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:838`) accepts only a **string**:

```ts
local_owner_session_id: typeof o.local_owner_session_id === 'string' ? o.local_owner_session_id : undefined,
```

The array is dropped → `ownerLeaseHeld`'s string clause is dead code, and the worker cannot tell
which session (or slot) holds the lease. This blocks the per-slot fix (WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28 child).

## Required behaviour

- Parse both shapes: legacy string and the current array. Normalise to a stable internal form
  (e.g. `local_owner_session_ids: string[]`) while keeping the legacy `string` field for
  compatibility with existing call sites.
- Fail-closed on an unparseable owner value (treat as ambiguous → busy), consistent with the rest
  of the parser.
- Keep per-slot `owner_session_id` parsing as-is (already string|null).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Unit test: legacy payload (`local_owner_session_id` string) parses and preserves the owner.
2. Unit test: current payload (2-element array) parses; the owner session is recovered (not
   `undefined`) and the URL element is ignored/handled deterministically.
3. Unit test: malformed owner (number/object/empty array) → fail-closed (busy / undefined), no throw.
4. A contract test pins the exact array shape observed from the live proxy
   (`["http://localhost:8080", "<session-id>"]`).
5. `fetchLocalStatus` never throws on either shape (poller result is a valid `LlamaStatus` or null).

## Notes

- Capture the fixture from `GET /llama/local/status`; the array shape was observed on
  2026-09-19 with proxy mode `cheap`, `total_slots=3`.
